text:
The tone of the email is currently too informal and abrupt for a professional academic context. It lacks a clear subject line, a polite opening, a specific request for a new deadline, and a professional closing. Additionally, the phrase "unforeseen personal circumstances" is vague; while you don't need to overshare, it is better to offer a brief, professional explanation or simply ask for the extension without over-explaining, while maintaining a respectful and appreciative tone.

Here is a revised version that matches a professional, respectful, and polite sentiment:

Subject: Request for Extension: Term Paper - [Your Name] - [Course Name/Number]

Dear Professor Smith,

I hope this email finds you well.

I am writing to respectfully request an extension on the deadline for my term paper, which is currently due on [Original Due Date]. Due to unforeseen personal circumstances, I have been unable to complete the paper to the standard I aim for by the original deadline.

I would be grateful if I could submit the paper by [Proposed New Date]. I understand the importance of deadlines and apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. I am committed to submitting high-quality work and appreciate your consideration of my request.

Thank you for your time and understanding.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]
[Your Student ID, if applicable]
